subject: why do i have to call fscores?

messages.subject: why do i have to call fscores?
parts:
Hi,

i have another question: as far as i understood, item parameters and ability estimates are usually estimated at the same time when i initially fit the model. Then why do i have to call fscores to estimate the ability? shouldn't those be already available after initial model estimation?

thanks!

ok, i reread about the estimation and mirt probably uses marginal maximum likelihood, right?

what about the distribution of ability, which is used in this approach? is this N(0,1) or the distribution of sum scores? Can one pass a distribution to the model estimation?

and, finally: i read in Millsap "statistical approaches to measurement invariance" that there is a method, where the model is reestimated, given a vector of thetas. is something like this possible in mirt?

thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: why do i have to call fscores?
parts:
On Sat, Dec 21, 2013 at 10:35 AM, <bea...@gmx.de> wrote:
> ok, i reread about the estimation and mirt probably uses marginal maximum likelihood, right?

Correct. The latent scores aren't estimated during estimation since
they are integrated over instead. Hence obtaining factor score
estimates is really a secondary thing, in the same way as traditional
factor analysis or SEM.

>
> what about the distribution of ability, which is used in this approach? is this N(0,1) or the distribution of sum scores? Can one pass a distribution to the model estimation?

Yes you can! As of the latest CRAN version (1.1) you can specify your
own function to determine the latent densities for the theta
integration grid. The default is (multivariate) Gaussian, or when
estimating via empirical histograms the latent distribution is
determined empirically.

>
> and, finally: i read in Millsap "statistical approaches to measurement invariance" that there is a method, where the model is reestimated, given a vector of thetas. is something like this possible in mirt?

I've never tried this approach, but the package certainly has the
tools to do it (the MHRM algorithm sounds very similar, so it wouldn't
take much to make it accommodate it). I don't have the book to know
the specifics, so I'll have to look for it sometime after the
holidays. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: why do i have to call fscores?
parts:
There isn't really an option to change this directly, though you could
modify the package code directly and reinstall it of course. The grid
is determined based on the number of quadpts, where larger points
results in a wider/more filled in grid symmetrically around 0.

Phil
